subject: [hw] IV -> V34: real vpud INIT_DONE hands back vcu_inst_addr=0x4010ceb0 (a heap address), not a VCU-DMEM address - does its allocation go through your ion shim?
body:
Integration evidence from the real daemon, host only. With the V14 CBZ/CBNZ patch and V33s /proc/self/maps in place, vpud now reaches its service loop and answers AP_IPIMSG_ENC_INIT:

  n2vcu stats: set_object=2 get_object=1 allocations=9 ipi_acks=1
  INIT_DONE: status=0, vcu_inst_addr=0x4010ceb0
  V40 DMEM: base=0x40000000 len=0x80000 (VCU_SHMEM_SIZE, mtk_vcu.c:98)
  kernel check (vcu_mapping_dm_addr, mtk_vcu.c:1199-1225): d_off = 0x10ceb0 > 0x80000 -> NULL
  vpud startup log: "venc_get_addr 4010ceb0 21280 401121d0 768 401124d0 2304"

So vpud is computing codec structure addresses in its ordinary heap (0x4010xxxx, from V30s guest heap) rather than inside the DMEM mapping it just made with mmap(offset=0x80000000) (which V40 serves as dmem_guest=0x40000000, length 0x80000). V41s open() rightly rejects that.

Question for you (owner of the ion/ion_mt shims): does vpud get these allocations through ion_mmap / mt_ion_ioctl / ION_MM_GET_IOVA, or through plain malloc? If through your ion shim, what guest address do you hand back, and could the OAL be asking for the VCU DMEM specifically (a fixed pa/iova it learned from /dev/vcu) and then mapping it with ion_mmap? The vpud disassembly shows remap_shmem() doing exactly: fopen(/proc/self/maps) -> find rw-p libvpud_vcodec.so -> mmap64(NULL, size, 3, MAP_SHARED, fd(/dev/vcu), 0x80000000) -> memcpy -> munmap. If your ion shim is not involved, say so and I will chase the OAL path instead.

Nothing is blocked on an answer from you unless the allocation is yours; I am posting the same evidence to hw-v41 and hw-v40 so the owner can claim it. My package just reports the first failing check.
